**Page Role & Rhythm Overview**
This is a deep-dive detail page — the buyer has already shown intent and needs to be drowned in trustworthy data, not coaxed with marketing fluff. The page runs 5 sections in a deliberate dense→denser→explosive→narrative→closing rhythm: a punchy header dashboard card, a tightly-packed mechanical specs grid, a full-bleed inspection scorecard "signature moment," a vertical timeline history scroll, and a closing CTA strip. No two sections share the same skeleton or surface treatment. The alternation is aggressive: dark purple → near-black grid → full-bleed magenta explosion → dark purple with lime timeline nodes → Midnight Lot CTA close.

**Signature Moment — Section 3 (Inspection Stats)**
The page's single most memorable visual move lives in the inspection stats section: a FULL-BLEED AOL Hot Magenta (#FF00CC) panel that breaks the purple/dark rhythm entirely, with the headline "THIS CAR PASSED." rendered in Arial Black at ~96px ALL-CAPS in Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00) with a hard black drop-shadow, bleeding off the left edge of the grid. The retro radial gauge / pixel-bar chart asset floats inside a beveled Bevel White (#E8E8E8) inset panel that overlaps the magenta background, crossing the section boundary line. This is a pure GeoCities maximalist moment — a saturated color block that screams "LOOK AT THIS SCORE" using the aesthetic's own visual aggression, not a modern SaaS callout box. Stat values are rendered in VT323 at oversized 48px (the one exception to the "accent only" rule for VT323 — justified here because these are literal dashboard readout numbers, not display headlines).

**Color & Surface Progression**
- Section 1 (Header): GeoCities Grape (#6600CC) background with a Midnight Lot (#110022) tiled-wallpaper texture overlay at low opacity. Bevel White raised panel for the dashboard card asset.

- Section 5 (CTA): Midnight Lot (#110022) background with a rainbow rule divider at the top edge. Netscape Lime (#00FF33) primary CTA button with beveled 3D treatment.

- Section 5 headline: Arial Black, ALL-CAPS, ~48px, Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00).
- All eyebrow labels: VT323, 13px, Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00) — consistent across page.

**Density & Whitespace Logic**
Section 1 is moderately padded (60px vertical) — it's an introduction, not a data dump. Section 2 is dense — tight 24px internal grid gaps, small cell padding, maximizing the "specs table" feel. Section 3 is explosively padded (80px vertical) to let the magenta breathe and the oversized type land. Section 4 uses generous vertical spacing between timeline nodes (48px gap) to let the narrative unfold. Section 5 is compact (48px vertical) — a closing strip, not a full section.

**Structural Ornament**
Rainbow rule dividers (6px height, CSS gradient across all 6 palette accent colors) appear between every section transition as a structural device — they are not decorative afterthoughts but literal section separators that reinforce the GeoCities-era page anatomy. An 88×31 "INSPECTED & CERTIFIED" badge sticker in Sunshine Honk with a Hot Magenta border appears in the top-right corner of Section 1's dashboard card. This page shares the GeoCities Grape / Midnight Lot surface alternation established on the Home page, uses the same rainbow rule dividers and 88×31 badge motifs, and maintains the VT323 eyebrow / hit-counter system. The beveled Bevel White panels echo the Browse Inventory card treatment. The Dial-Up Sky hyperlink color appears on all inline text links. This page is the most data-dense in the site — it earns that density because the buyer is here to verify, not to be sold.",

### Page Role & Tone
This is the visual confidence page — the buyer has already read specs and now needs to *see* the car with their own eyes. **The Signature Moment lives in the Exterior Gallery section (Section 2): a full-bleed, top-down pixel-art orthographic diagram of the sedan — rendered in AOL Hot Magenta (#FF00CC) outlines on a deep Midnight Lot (#110022) surface — that BLEEDS across the full page width and sits BEHIND a transparent overlay of photo-count badges and category labels.** The diagram is oversized, spanning the full 12-column grid, with numbered hotspot markers in Netscape Lime (#00FF33) punching out of the magenta line art. This is unmistakably 90s-web energy: a technical diagram treated as a hero image, overlaid with beveled badge widgets like stickers slapped onto a poster. No modern SaaS page would do this. It belongs to this aesthetic because GeoCities users loved putting technical diagrams and pixel art as page centerpieces, and the Dashboard Product layout family calls for data-rich visual modules. The diagram functions structurally — it maps the exterior photo categories spatially — not decoratively.

1. **Page Header** — Dense masthead strip: dark Midnight Lot bar, all-caps Arial Black headline, breadcrumb navigation, two beveled CTA buttons. Compact and directional. Sets the portal-header energy immediately.

- **Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00)** appears on: photo-count chip labels, the oversized "47" in Section 5, and the "UNDER CONSTRUCTION" motif badge in Section 1.
- **Browser Chrome Gray (#C0C0C0)** appears on: beveled button shadows, panel inset borders, and table row stripes in the side-tab rail.

### Rainbow Rule Dividers
Every section boundary is separated by a full-width rainbow rule divider — a horizontal band of 4px stripes cycling through Netscape Lime → AOL Hot Magenta → Dial-Up Sky → Sunshine Honk. - **H1 (Section 1)**: Arial Black, ALL-CAPS, 64px, Netscape Lime, -0.02em tracking, hard white drop-shadow offset 3px/3px.

      "page_level_design_instruction": "## RevvLot — Photo Gallery Page: Full Design Direction

### Page Role & Tone
This is the visual confidence page — the buyer has already read specs and now needs to *see* the car with their own eyes. The design must feel like opening a GeoCities photo album from 1998 that somehow got turbocharged: beveled panels, tiled wallpaper, rainbow rule dividers, and category tabs that feel ripped from an old Netscape browser window. Every section should feel like a different "room" in a 90s web portal, yet all unified by the shared dark-purple/lime/magenta palette.

### Signature Moment
**The Signature Moment lives in the Exterior Gallery section (Section 2): a full-bleed, top-down pixel-art orthographic diagram of the sedan — rendered in AOL Hot Magenta (#FF00CC) outlines on a deep Midnight Lot (#110022) surface — that BLEEDS across the full page width and sits BEHIND a transparent overlay of photo-count badges and category labels.** The diagram is oversized, spanning the full 12-column grid, with numbered hotspot markers in Netscape Lime (#00FF33) punching out of the magenta line art. This is unmistakably 90s-web energy: a technical diagram treated as a hero image, overlaid with beveled badge widgets like stickers slapped onto a poster. No modern SaaS page would do this. It belongs to this aesthetic because GeoCities users loved putting technical diagrams and pixel art as page centerpieces, and the Dashboard Product layout family calls for data-rich visual modules. The diagram functions structurally — it maps the exterior photo categories spatially — not decoratively.

### Section Sequence & Rhythm
1. **Page Header** — Dense masthead strip: dark Midnight Lot bar, all-caps Arial Black headline, breadcrumb navigation, two beveled CTA buttons. Compact and directional. Sets the portal-header energy immediately.
2. **Exterior Gallery** — SIGNATURE MOMENT. Full-bleed pixel-art diagram behind the grid. Four photo-category panels arranged in a 2×2 beveled card grid below the diagram. Maximum density and visual aggression.
3. **Interior Gallery** — Side-tabbed layout: a vertical tab rail on the left (Browser-Chrome Gray, beveled) with four category tabs; the active tab's photo grid expands right. Alternates the rhythm from Section 2's full-bleed chaos to a structured dashboard panel feel.
4. **Mechanical Gallery** — Three-column feature panel with retro pixel icons above each column header, dense copy below. Dark GeoCities Grape (#6600CC) surface to break the page's background alternation. Feels like a diagnostic readout panel.
5. **CTA Close** — Centered, high-contrast, full-bleed Midnight Lot panel with a massive Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00) numeral "47" dominating the left half and the reserve CTA on the right. Asymmetric typographic stunt. Sparse after the density of Sections 2–4.

### Color & Surface Logic
- **Page background tiling**: The entire page sits on a tiled micro-pattern wallpaper in GeoCities Grape (#6600CC) — a subtle repeating diamond/dot tile at low opacity over the solid purple, visible between sections. This is the page's ground texture.
- **Section surfaces alternate**: Section 1 = Midnight Lot (#110022). Section 2 = Midnight Lot with the magenta diagram bleeding behind. Section 3 = Bevel White (#E8E8E8) panels on a dark Midnight Lot rail. Section 4 = GeoCities Grape (#6600CC) solid. Section 5 = Midnight Lot (#110022).
- **Netscape Lime (#00FF33)** appears on: active states, photo-count badges, hotspot markers, primary CTA buttons, and the "47 Photos" numeral in Section 5.
- **AOL Hot Magenta (#FF00CC)** appears on: the exterior diagram outlines, rainbow rule dividers between sections, the Section 5 eyebrow label, and badge borders throughout.
- **Dial-Up Sky (#00CCFF)** appears on: hyperlinks, metric card borders, tab borders, and the "PHOTO GALLERY" eyebrow labels.
- **Sunshine Honk (#FFFF00)** appears on: photo-count chip labels, the oversized "47" in Section 5, and the "UNDER CONSTRUCTION" motif badge in Section 1.
- **Browser Chrome Gray (#C0C0C0)** appears on: beveled button shadows, panel inset borders, and table row stripes in the side-tab rail.

### Rainbow Rule Dividers
Every section boundary is separated by a full-width rainbow rule divider — a horizontal band of 4px stripes cycling through Netscape Lime → AOL Hot Magenta → Dial-Up Sky → Sunshine Honk. This is a structural device, not decorative trim. It signals section transitions exactly as 90s web pages used <HR> tags with rainbow GIF replacements.

### Typography Hierarchy
- **H1 (Section 1)**: Arial Black, ALL-CAPS, 64px, Netscape Lime, -0.02em tracking, hard white drop-shadow offset 3px/3px.
- **H2 (Sections 2–4)**: Arial Black, ALL-CAPS, 40px, alternating between AOL Hot Magenta (Sections 2, 4) and Dial-Up Sky (Section 3).
- **H2 (Section 5)**: Arial Black, ALL-CAPS, 52px, Bevel White (#E8E8E8), centered.
- **Eyebrow labels**: VT323 pixel font, 13px, Sunshine Honk or Dial-Up Sky, all-caps, letter-spaced 0.15em — used strictly as small category tags above headlines.
- **Body / descriptions**: Verdana, 14px, 1.65 line-height, Bevel White or Browser Chrome Gray on dark surfaces.
- **Photo-count badges**: VT323, 12px, Netscape Lime text on Midnight Lot pill badges with Netscape Lime border.
- **Oversized "47" in Section 5**: Arial Black, 200px, Sunshine Honk, positioned left-half of the panel, partially cropped by the right edge of its column — a typographic bleed move.

### Density / Whitespace Logic
- Sections 1 and 5 are relatively sparse — tight vertical padding (40px top/bottom), focused on a single action or statement.
- Sections 2, 3, and 4 are dense — photo grids, tab rails, icon columns, and category copy pack the panel tightly with 24px internal gutters between cards.
- The overall rhythm is: TIGHT → DENSE → DENSE → DENSE → SPARSE. This mirrors the user journey: arrive quickly, dig deep into photos, then emerge to a clear decision moment.

### Responsive Behavior
- Mobile (< 768px): The Section 2 pixel-art diagram collapses to a centered 320px wide version above the photo cards; the 2×2 card grid stacks to a single column. The Section 3 side-tab rail collapses to a horizontal scrollable tab strip above the photo grid. Section 4 three-column layout stacks vertically. Section 5 stacks the "47" numeral above the CTA block, both centered.
- Tablet (768–1024px): Section 2 diagram scales to full width at reduced height. Section 3 tab rail stays vertical but narrows. Section 4 goes 3-column. Section 5 maintains the asymmetric split.
- Desktop (> 1024px): Full 12-column grid, all layouts as described in section plans.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses every color token in the shared palette at least once, applies Arial Black/Verdana/VT323 at their specified scales, and reinforces the beveled-panel, tiled-wallpaper, rainbow-rule, and 88x31-badge visual cues from the aesthetic guidance. It is the most visually documentation-heavy page in the site (photo gallery), so it leans into the Dashboard Product layout family's "data modules and feature panels" structure more than any other page — but always filtered through the 90s web portal lens.",

**Pages (5):** `index.html`, `product.html`, `specs.html`, `gallery.html`, `reserve.html` — each with `data-page-slug` on `<body>` and all blueprint section ids (e.g. `home-section-1` … `reserve-section-5`) plus `data-section-type` on every section.
